distinguishing_features: Direct Transfer of thermal inertia via a localized thermal mass block to homogenize thermal gradients at the clamp joint
Replacement of compliant mechanical interfaces with a passive, high-conductivity solid insert to reduce cyclic thermal differential
Use of a high-volume, high-conductivity metal block (>10 cm³, >50 W/mK) to increase thermal diffusion time relative to cycle period
Mechanism targets reduction of ΔT_local at the joint interface through enhanced conduction, not through monitoring or operational derating
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reducing cyclic thermal stress at turbofan bleed-air duct clamp joints caused by transient thermal gradients without relying on flexible joints or active control systems
parsed.viable_reason: The solution uses physically realizable materials and principles of heat conduction to demonstrably reduce thermal gradients within operational time scales.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The shift from mechanical compliance or monitoring to thermal inertia management via a conductive mass is not an obvious extension of prior art focused on sensing, derating, or flexible joints.
